maps.name: Mirefen
maps.subtitle: Misty fen of boardwalks and stilt villages

props.text: West: Lowlantern, then the Sinking Mere and the Heron Bridge. North-west, past the Croaking Stones: the old moon-gate. (Scratched underneath, in a careful hand: PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE CROCOLISKS. THEY ARE FED.)
A dead lamp-post. Its hook is empty and its jar is smashed.
A dead lamp-post. Its hook is empty and its jar is smashed.
A dead lamp-post. Its hook is empty and its jar is smashed.
A dead lamp-post. Its hook is empty and its jar is smashed.
A stone lantern, sunk to its shoulders in black water.
A stone lantern leaning in the mere, its fire-box full of weed.
A drowned lantern, a skein of something knotted round its foot.
Granny Sen's lantern. Somebody has wound a fresh ribbon round its neck.
Under the willow: crushed clover and a scatter of beetle-wings.
The Low Bell still hangs in the broken arch: green bronze, cracked lip, a rope of rotten reeds.
A giant toadstool. The soil round its foot smells of rain on a cellar door.
A giant toadstool. The soil round its foot smells of rain on a cellar door.
A giant toadstool. The soil round its foot smells of rain on a cellar door.
A fairy ring of fat speckled toadstools. In the middle, a flat stone, still warm from something small sitting on it.
A coven totem: driftwood, an antlered skull, green fire in the sockets. The mirelings bow to it when they pass.
A coven totem hung with frog-bone charms. It hums, very faintly, in a voice that is not a frog's.
A coven totem at the edge of the reeds. Someone has left it a dead eel, very respectfully.
A coven totem on the old road to the moon-gate. The reeds lean away from it.
A mireling stewpot on a reed fire. Something in it is singing, indignantly.
A serene stone face sinking into the mire, one hand still raised above the water with a lantern in it.

regions.name: Lowlantern
regions.text: Lowlantern — a stilt village on a pool of lilies. Every porch has a lantern hook. Most of the hooks are empty.

regions.name: Sinking Mere
regions.text: The Sinking Mere — where Lowlantern sends its lights. The water is very still, and full of stone lanterns.

regions.name: Drowned Barrows
regions.text: The Drowned Barrows — the fen's old burial mounds, going under one cairn at a time. Something squelches, then stops.

regions.name: Croaking Stones
regions.text: The Croaking Stones — mireling country. A hundred golden eyes blink at you from the reeds, then a hundred more.

regions.name: Moon-Gate
regions.text: The old moon-gate stands in the reeds, turning slowly inside like a held breath. The coven's totems face it, not you.

regions.name: Sunken Statue
regions.successText: Water is running somewhere it shouldn't — down. Under the statue's raised hand, moss hides a stair cut into the mire.
regions.failText: The statue gazes over the water. Frogs. Reeds. Nothing else you can see.

regions.name: Willow Hollow
regions.text: Willow Hollow — giant toadstools and weeping willows. The air smells of rain and something sweet.

regions.name: Gnashing Shallows
regions.text: The Gnashing Shallows. The logs here have eyes.

regions.name: Heron Bridge
regions.successText: A heron is carved on the bridge's keystone — and under the downstream arch, someone has wedged an oilskin bundle out of sight.
regions.failText: An old heron is carved on the keystone, worn almost smooth.

quests.name: The Drowned Lanterns
quests.summary: Penhallow's records speak of lanterns sunk in the fens of Mirefen. Find out what drowned them.

stages.description: Go west from Brightwater into the fens of Mirefen.
Find the Reeve of Lowlantern, the stilt village on the lily pool, and ask about the drowned lanterns.
Search the drowned lanterns of the Sinking Mere, west along the Fen Road. Whatever is holding them down, cut it loose and bring it back.

objectives.text: Drowning cords cut from the Sinking Mere

stages.description: Show the drowning cords to Reeve Tamsin in Lowlantern.

objectives.text: Show the cords to Reeve Tamsin

stages.description: Mother Mire's coven gathers at the old moon-gate in the north-west of the fen. Find Auntie Gall, Eldest of the Coven, and stop the drowning at its root.
The hooks are out of the water. Go back to the Sinking Mere: there is someone on the boardwalk who has been waiting a long time for the end of a song.
Bring word back to Archivist Penhallow in Brightwater.
